manifest.title: Narrated Recording to Tutorial
manifest.summary: Turn an uploaded screen recording with original spoken explanation into a trimmed, subtitled widescreen tutorial with chapter timestamps.
manifest.use_when: Turn an uploaded screen recording with original spoken explanation into a trimmed, subtitled widescreen tutorial with chapter timestamps.
manifest.description:
Example — cafe new-hire onboarding: a manager uploads a narrated walkthrough of the order desk. Produce one widescreen tutorial covering receipt, acceptance, readiness and handoff, with chapter timestamps and editable subtitles. Keep the source, production versions and review outcome together as the training changes.

These are video-production Workspaces, not order-management systems or POS integrations.

Upload one MP4/MOV/WebM with picture and original spoken audio, 10 seconds to 30 minutes long, to this Workspace's Knowledge. Provide its Knowledge path, optionally its matching SRT path, and the desired focus. Only use recordings you may process; remove sensitive material first. Requires writable Workspace storage, worker FFmpeg/ffprobe with libass, and your configured AI model. Without an SRT, a timestamp-capable STT route and its normal credits or BYOK key are also required. Text-only STT is a blocker, never replaced with invented timestamps. Supplied SRT timing is not independently verified. Long captions are split proportionally within their source cue.

Select up to 12 chronological, non-overlapping chapters totaling 10–600 seconds. Keep the problem, prerequisites, demonstrated steps and outcome; trim unrelated chatter. Keep full spoken instructions and the intervening source footage. Never reorder operations, invent product capabilities or claim that transcript-only evidence proves a visible UI state. Name chapters from the speaker's explanation. The operator must check the actual footage. The renderer fits the whole screen in 1280x720 and retains original speech; no replacement narration.

Start from Workspace Chat or the installed Flow. The pipeline inspects the source, loads/transcribes speech, selects complete cue ranges, renders real subtitled MP4s, writes SRT, chapter/edit JSON and a frame preview, runs deterministic checks, and pauses for your playback acceptance. Each output has a durable Knowledge document link.

No silent-recording voiceover, automatic redaction, subject tracking, URL downloading, music, external publishing, account connection or scheduled background work. Machine QA verifies decoding, dimensions, duration, audio-stream presence and subtitle timing, not factual accuracy, speech intelligibility, privacy or visual readability. Watch every final video before accepting. Reject to retain the package for revision; rerun with corrected source/SRT or a revised focus. Retries create new output folders and keep earlier artifacts.

Simulation is a walkthrough only: it does not transcribe, render or spend media credits.
